annotations.title: A man that is an Heretike.
annotations.text: [1] Not euery one that erreth in religion, is an Heretike, but he onely that after the Churches determination, wilfully and stubburnely standeth in his false opinion, not yelding to decree of Councel or the cheefe Pastors of the Church therein. They (saith S. Augustine ep. 162.) that defend their sentence (though false and peruerse) with no stubburne stomake or obstinate hart, specially if it be such as them selues by bold presumption broched not, but receiued it of their deceiued parents, and do seeke the truth warily and carefully, being ready to be reformed if they finde it, such are not to be reputed among Heretikes. And againe, li. 18 de Ciuit. c. 51. [2] They that in the Church of Christ haue any crased or peruerse opinion, if being admonished to be of a sound and right opinion, they resist obstinatly, and wil not amend their pestiferous opinions, but persist in defense of them, are thereby become Heretikes, and going forth out of the Church, are counted for enimies that exercise vs. Againe li. 4 de Bapt. cont. Donat. c. 16. He is an Heretike that, when the doctrine of the Catholike faith is made plaine and manifest vnto him, had rather resist it, and choose that which him self held &c. And in diuers places he declareth that S. Cyprian, though he held an errour, yet was no Heretike, because he would not haue defended it after a general Council had declared it to be an errour. li. 2 de bapt. c. 4. So Possidonius in the life of S. Augustine [3] reporteth, how, after the determination of the See Apostolike that Pelagius opinion was heretical, al men esteemed Pelagius an Heretike, and the Emperour made lawes against him as against an Heretike. Againe S. Augustine saith, He is an Heretike in my opinion, that for some temporal commoditie, and specially for his glorie and principalitie, coineth or els foloweth false or new opinions. de vtilit. credendi cap. 1. [4] Let our Protestants behold them selues in this glasse, and withal let them marke al other proprieties that old Heretikes euer had, and they shal finde al definitions and markes of an Heretike to fall vpon them selues. And therfore they must not maruel if we warne al Catholike men by the wordes of the Apostle in this place, to take heede of them, and to shunne their preachings, bookes, conuenticles and companies. [5] Neither neede the people be curious to knowe what they say, much lesse to confute them: but they must trust Gods Church, which doth refute and condemne them. And it is ynough for them to knowe that they be condemned, as S Augustine noteth in the later end of his booke de heresibus. And S. Cyprian [6] saith notably to Antonianus demaunding curiously what heresies Nouatianus did teach: No matter, quoth he, What heresies he hath or teacheth, when he teacheth without, that is to say, out of the Church.

The former markes agree to the Protestants.
Their bookes, seruice, & preaching must be auoided.

annotations.title: Subuerted.
annotations.text: ◦ Heretikes are often incorrigible, yet the Church of God ceaseth not by al meanes possible to reuoke them. therfore S. Augustine saith ep. 162. The Heretike him self though swelling with odious and detestable pride, and madde with the frowardnes of wicked contention, as We admonish that he be auoided lest he deceiue the weaklings and litle ones, so we refuse not by al meanes possible to seeke his amendment and reformation.

notes.text: The Church seeketh the amendement of the most obstinate Heretikes.

annotations.title: By his owne iudgement.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Other greuous offenders be separated by excommunication from the communion of Saincts and the fellowship of Gods Church, by the sentence of their Superiors in the same Church: but Heretikes more miserable and infortunate then they, runne out of the Church of their owne accord, and so giue sentence against their owne soules to damnation.

notes.text: Heretikes cut them selues frō the Church.
